invalid.because: `primitive` is `chip`, which names a part rather than one of the eight primitives
`primitive` is missing altogether, so nothing keys on it
`class` carries the variant token but not the primitive token `qe-dv-chips`
`class` is not normalised: a double space, so token matching by split is unsafe
`class` carries every token but in the wrong order: the family, primitive and variant tokens come first and in that order
`class` repeats the `qe-dv` family token as an author token; the directive drops a token already present, so a repeat is a defect rather than a harmless duplicate
`class` carries a second variant token in the author tail; the variant is derived from the property, and the directive drops any author token that is itself a variant token
`tone` is a colour name rather than a member of the closed tone vocabulary
`class` says `--pill` while `variant` is `tag`: the derived token disagrees with the property
an item carries neither `id` nor `label`, so the chip has nothing to render
an item carries an unrecognised field, which the contract treats as a violation rather than a private extension
an item `tone` is a number rather than one of the five tone strings
`items` is non-empty but the fallback list has no items: an empty container with the data hidden in props
`items` has two entries but the fallback list has one: the props and the children disagree, which is the one defect the whole contract exists to prevent
the fallback list carries a third chip span that no entry of `items` accounts for, so the page shows a chip the data does not have
the fallback holds a bare text node instead of a chip span, so the children no longer render the data
a chip span carries a tone token that disagrees with the set's resolved `tone`
`contract` is a number rather than the version string
`mark` is a word rather than a glyph
`items` is empty but the fallback is a list rather than the empty-set notice
a chip span re-describes itself with `contract`, `primitive`, `part` and a duplicate `chip` object; an inner node carries a class and nothing else, and the datum lives exactly twice
a chip span carries a top-level `label`, which `myst-cli`'s embed transform deletes; no node this primitive emits carries `label`, `identifier` or `html_id`
an item's `tone` differs from the set's; contract 1.0 resolves one tone onto every chip and has no per-chip override

the root carries a top-level `label`; `myst-cli`'s embed transform runs `selectAll('[identifier],[label],[html_id]')` over an embedded subtree and deletes all three from every node whose type is not `crossReference`, `cite`, `footnoteDefinition`, `footnoteReference`, `captionNumber` or `link`, so the property works locally and silently disappears the first time the page is embedded elsewhere

the retired `naLabel` is carried on the root: the draft let each block spell a missing value for itself, contract 1.0 spells it one way — `null` in the properties, an em dash in the fallback — so a node still carrying the option sends a consumer looking for a string that means nothing
